Ryan Kominakis opened his energy bill several months ago and decided on the
spot to run for state representative in Indiana’s 4th District.

He saw his bill double virtually overnight because of exorbitant rate
increases, which ultimately forced some financially strapped consumers to
[turn off the lights, lower the thermostat, and
shiver](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BMPB2IwN9YVV8nzHPJYIBOia-2F1Q-2BS0pY-2BFLIj8YHL4Qc8KR3uPL2DYDxlrB06SCGbPbBl1-2B00QT7QoapEc-2FXtdQ5Tbkg8DVj4lSS9f3MglsqIgmhF-2BBs0Sjl20W6idrwSSfygCrHMo7jmDO7pk2XYyhAClXYIHPraYZE-2FV2y6GSO4vyB_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRq8Z9ffsYIv9ofdZclCmAP8Yx3zmiwSVWQmVptIyXa1rsJpSvIa3X9fBPOIgNoaCH6Jcgb79PJZ2bmhOeUO9sWABtPEBw1-2BeGI5uoQBQ9d7zJ-2B-2BDMfezLQH5YGknXTxm8jb2jEmBMAqCjewJGT6Fdy751w3Ry-2BbVupWM0AcLHTKTMN9urd0qpueUg2MaKqywp09DhSaXLfjhkI7HSG5atcunaumqdvmT8m6emyKeN1g83MkGvfopT-2F0bDD5qmGD0iLjuD5MeLmGrQPHD96bXS-2BYr4oOwygVD-2FasvtIFTAjHWuyiVpGRzV-2BiQ0WDBfGaQK5LqTfL4wnAt-2FvgscyANpvCnvDbNb34coHcgX0CQOAaGZmtWql-2BonIIKeByZY48PciIILEpFltgin4Hf-2BaMudTaHtMJkssKxzWfE9nAFVGJXlxgnR3nioGGVLFdZV2pP1JYbdiOW2bAcWqzbfp67v-2FKcGYyHwj86K27CRun0UxKf2q3h-2FtuPoiEoM08Rp8lLdfbh-2FqizMCGblsM7gWhFE5fXUgmUmV6-2FX1TGoDP7WdbC2fn6kAyEUnMAzGP3oPK8NGzRIN-2FYj4OKlljWYeq3G3s1UWDOMR2C8jQ4fMDvJ5x0w74Isk8KXSh5s9TrdYsH8Cf1ciRdc0w4jF5-2Fk6V6ldZ6yI1Z1m7EkiaGIPVPuDil6PmpQ64avZoUSO1DhNcM0s75I6scsJIFCc0GQQ3Q3qw-3D)

with United Steelworkers (USW) Local 1066 at U.S. Steel’s Gary Works, long ago
tired of watching the state’s corporate-friendly leaders give [huge tax breaks
to the
wealthy](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BE2ZK0hStH4TdeMFKQyhfuhPSDbW7ndYaK3hXl1JdjdotCAPk7NSfbE3VevKZuEGDwoypuANrWFDkB3AHynu5j5KKbfz5Ggpjb3jXR2rEAemc-2FZGtHsfSQolYmAZoYENYg-3D-3DCTjy_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRq8Z9ffsYIv9ofdZclCmAP8Yx3zmiwSVWQmVptIyXa1rsJpSvIa3X9fBPOIgNoaCH6Jcgb79PJZ2bmhOeUO9sWABtPEBw1-2BeGI5uoQBQ9d7zJ-2B-2BDMfezLQH5YGknXTxm8jb2jEmBMAqCjewJGT6Fdy751w3Ry-2BbVupWM0AcLHTKTMN9urd0qpueUg2MaKqywp09DhSaXLfjhkI7HSG5atcunaumqdvmT8m6emyKeN1g83MkGvfopT-2F0bDD5qmGD0iLjuD5MeLmGrQPHD96bXS-2BYr4oOwygVD-2FasvtIFTAjHWuyiVpGRzV-2BiQ0WDBfGaQK5LqTfL4wnAt-2FvgscyANpvCnvDbNb34coHcgX0CQOAaGZmtWql-2BonIIKeByZY48PciIILEpFltgin4Hf-2BaMudTaHtMJkssKxzWfE9nAFVGJXlxgnR3nioGGVLFdZV2pP1JYbdiOW2bAcWqzbfp67v-2FKcGYyHwj86K27CRun0UxKf2q3h-2FtuPoiEoM08Rp8lLdRpaul4n2uq4NfOXoapq9A6kFA-2BqoTF4n4fOO9-2B62YDCzOHDBd8JYEzLhnSPK8Phem6aD4GGh1Jb8Dkzf6xV4NbUTe82cNBB3VXlWEPWk0VVUDjlQRJ0ZZw-2BRs5RexgK2rX8vAOoBysdMU9JQ0rm85jKN1OvAk22SycRCxQUE2U3Vaw9O7ZPYUnTqGApXkCqNblA31rm-2F53DfkeYVRvAWFI-3D)

He realized what’s becoming clearer and clearer to working people. We have to
elect more of our own to public office if we want a government that works for
us.

“I still work 12-hour shifts and swing shifts on the shop floor,” Ryan said,
highlighting the credentials setting him apart from his opponent, a 20-year
incumbent and former airline industry vice president who once referred to
members of the public as “[noise
boxes](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BPGJRjtgjXXghrXtj7gNJh96yLJD4y13Qp-2F87-2F-2FdCBwqlzogyyNGt0R-2BQIpCfEp9MPbuU-2BkutnG46wsUlOW73-2F71TgjIu8LCND7TCal66CgrCeZuSKX-2FiHh1-2B3OLK72ehpxN2s-2B4uT3giF-2B8-2BRy-2BwfoJUyZkJtIq25ANghjbNiDI-

all cost more,” he said. Yet, he points out, his opponent ignores these
struggles and “legislates like a corporate executive,” even threatening to
derail a town’s funding after the mayor criticized the skyrocketing utility
bills.

This is what happens when the privileged elbow their way into office to serve
themselves and others of their ilk, throwing everyone else under the bus.

It’s so pervasive that many of us no longer have true representation,
[according to a 2024
study](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BMexydBIy1sXq1XNbinjkIyC5aCIPrOYYb2H12hgnHUAdaj8KEUIF-2F2R4Lu-2BptWZJFeoFLetgMQ9DVXWN1tIhxQed0YIusE5pCEAm-2FBi5-2BjR2Xdo_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRq8Z9ffsYIv9ofdZclCmAP8Yx3zmiwSVWQmVptIyXa1rsJpSvIa3X9fBPOIgNoaCH6Jcgb79PJZ2bmhOeUO9sWABtPEBw1-2BeGI5uoQBQ9d7zJ-2B-2BDMfezLQH5YGknXTxm8jb2jEmBMAqCjewJGT6Fdy751w3Ry-2BbVupWM0AcLHTKTMN9urd0qpueUg2MaKqywp09DhSaXLfjhkI7HSG5atcunaumqdvmT8m6emyKeN1g83MkGvfopT-2F0bDD5qmGD0iLjuD5MeLmGrQPHD96bXS-2BYr4oOwygVD-2FasvtIFTAjHWuyiVpGRzV-2BiQ0WDBfGaQK5LqTfL4wnAt-2FvgscyANpvCnvDbNb34coHcgX0CQOAaGZmtWql-2BonIIKeByZY48PciIILEpFltgin4Hf-2BaMudTaHtMJkssKxzWfE9nAFVGJXlxgnR3nioGGVLFdZV2pP1JYbdiOW2bAcWqzbfp67v-2FKcGYyHwj86K27CRun0UxKf2q3h-2FtuPoiEoM08Rp8lLdVFTRcIhmbbBULQSxj73Vp-2F0yY8JJxk-2FlY4AChPbWGYXQNk-2Fc5yWYpvgfx5jH-2BFf-2F0N-2FMinRHyuVdPKjWOMU2oktqZDjdSQQsvGEDBdGhS2E5mF-2BaatwF4S5QLN64jOMhxewUJgjFcyPjnawJCOCM96KUeiBe4rKvjPFXb8a8DMLlarlI5EOh0Sp6LWtrpAuRL0gFnSVQ11nwzT-2B3TCyVrg-3D)
from Duke University and Loyola University Chicago that showed how thoroughly
the rich have wormed their way into power and how urgently we need to reclaim
it.

About half of the US workforce is made up of mechanics, glassmakers,
autoworkers, miners, steelworkers, other manufacturing workers and so on. Yet
less than [2
percent](https://u36605228.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click?upn=u001.irwnA1ZB8N-2BHNL3jUmYY-2BMexydBIy1sXq1XNbinjkIyC5aCIPrOYYb2H12hgnHUAdaj8KEUIF-2F2R4Lu-2BptWZJFeoFLetgMQ9DVXWN1tIhxQed0YIusE5pCEAm-2FBi5-2BjR3V3g_pb-2B40bGv8VszgSLSxZSae2hniLAOGi35ajohLqdIu8wIVCP-2FjsifAGPrnz8TzLY-2Bsd55T98Nf4Mouz9Lb09iRq8Z9ffsYIv9ofdZclCmAP8Yx3zmiwSVWQmVptIyXa1rsJpSvIa3X9fBPOIgNoaCH6Jcgb79PJZ2bmhOeUO9sWABtPEBw1-2BeGI5uoQBQ9d7zJ-2B-2BDMfezLQH5YGknXTxm8jb2jEmBMAqCjewJGT6Fdy751w3Ry-2BbVupWM0AcLHTKTMN9urd0qpueUg2MaKqywp09DhSaXLfjhkI7HSG5atcunaumqdvmT8m6emyKeN1g83MkGvfopT-2F0bDD5qmGD0iLjuD5MeLmGrQPHD96bXS-2BYr4oOwygVD-2FasvtIFTAjHWuyiVpGRzV-2BiQ0WDBfGaQK5LqTfL4wnAt-2FvgscyANpvCnvDbNb34coHcgX0CQOAaGZmtWql-2BonIIKeByZY48PciIILEpFltgin4Hf-2BaMudTaHtMJkssKxzWfE9nAFVGJXlxgnR3nioGGVLFdZV2pP1JYbdiOW2bAcWqzbfp67v-2FKcGYyHwj86K27CRun0UxKf2q3h-2FtuPoiEoM08Rp8lLdVfpdbcx4RPWXFUfGZePw2SXX3Pj-2B4Eo4pMzg-2FjrzyBnP8PgqudzeCFgfibi3GIFKxn92J0-2FVkqRKo9Nnk3vzDYiPMBI6ka9seQLdEiHJzkhwBTUm187BgVXdC5YJAcWo3Wk7eke36AIbhTwhx0mRP6ZrwlRjZKr5SUVGO-2BKA5jZOnoNwX2fKXtdDuxvR73mPxV2fDEl-2FsUrZqbPp6wcds4-3D)
of state lawmakers across the country hailed from working-class backgrounds as
of 2023, the researchers determined.

Just 116 of the 7,300 lawmakers in the study “currently or last worked in
manual labor, service industry, clerical or labor union jobs.” In 10 states,
the researchers found not a single lawmaker with a real, working person’s job.

Working people, especially union leaders like Ryan, never hide from a problem
or try to wish it away. They face a challenge head-on and get the job done,
delivering results because their paychecks, their families, and their very
lives in dangerous workplaces depend on it.

Ryan, who’s worked as a crew leader and safety advocate, looks after his
coworkers. The same concern for others also fuels his civic involvement,
including volunteer work with the Veterans of Foreign Wars, an organization of
fellow combat veterans facing the same kinds of challenges that he does.

It’s the kind of mindset—the kind of skillset—ideal for public office.

“You know how to be a leader,” Ryan said of his union activism. “When you work
with management, that’s kind of like reaching across the aisle, working with
the other side.”

The data backs him up.

Union members also use their leadership skills to build bridges in the
government arena. They convert their experience in the trenches into
credibility in the halls of power. And they win voters’ trust in ways that
drive turnout at the polls, the researchers concluded.

As Ryan decided in running for the Indiana legislature, there’s only one way
to ensure working people get the government we deserve.

We have to build it with our own hands.
